meaning: Do not stay upset about something that has already happened and cannot be changed. Learn from it and move on.

questions.sentence: You cannot get back the game you lost yesterday, so ____. Practise for the next one instead!
"____," Mum said. "The broken vase cannot be repaired, but you can be more careful next time."
I sent the birthday card to the wrong address. Dad said, "____. Let's send another one today."

meaning: In a difficult situation or stuck with a problem.

questions.sentence: I was ____ when I reached the bus stop and realised I had neither my travel card nor any money.
Our group was ____ because the presentation was due that morning and nobody had brought the poster.
Ben found himself ____ when he locked the front door with his keys still inside the empty house.

meaning: An extra good thing that makes an already good situation even better.

questions.sentence: Winning the art competition was wonderful, and meeting my favourite artist afterwards was ____.
We already loved our new flat. Discovering a lovely playground next door was ____.
The class enjoyed a fantastic day at the zoo. Getting a free animal book on the way out was ____.

meaning: A playful name for someone who is clumsy and often drops things. Use it kindly, not to tease someone who is upset.

questions.sentence: After I dropped the ball for the third time, I laughed at myself and said, "I'm such a ____ today!"
"What a ____ I am!" said Dad with a smile as he dropped another sock while carrying the washing.
After dropping both her pencil and her rubber, Lily joked, "Call me ____! I cannot seem to hold on to anything today."

meaning: Something I do not enjoy or am not interested in. Change 'my' to 'your', 'her', 'his' or another suitable word when needed.

questions.sentence: I would rather read a mystery book; watching football is ____.
"Camping is ____," I explained. "I do not enjoy sleeping in a tent."
I know many people love very spicy food, but it is ____ because I do not enjoy the burning taste.

meaning: Being very careful about what you say or do because you are afraid of upsetting someone. 'Eggshells' is also commonly written as one word.

questions.sentence: Everyone was ____ around the grumpy coach, choosing each word carefully so that he would not get angry.
I felt as though I was ____ when I asked my upset friend about our argument, afraid that I might hurt her feelings again.
The children were ____ around their older sister, who was in a bad mood and became cross at the smallest comment.

meaning: Continue doing something at the same good rate or standard. Put the activity or object between 'keep' and 'up': keep the good work up.

questions.sentence: You have set a good pace for the charity walk. Try to ____ until you reach the finish line.
Our team has been playing well. We must ____ for the rest of the match.
Ella practised the piano every day last month, and she ____ throughout this month too, continuing the same routine.

meaning: Not tell someone about something; keep information secret from them. For example: keep the surprise from Tom. In this worksheet it means hiding information, rather than preventing an action.

questions.sentence: We are planning a surprise party for Mum. Please ____ so that she does not find out before Saturday.
Sam trusted me with his secret. I promised to ____ because he did not want anyone else to know.
The children bought Dad a present last week and ____ until his birthday yesterday, so he had no idea what they had chosen.

meaning: Check or examine something, such as a piece of homework. With a pronoun, say 'look it over', not 'look over it'.

questions.sentence: I have finished my spelling homework. Could you ____ and check for mistakes before I hand it in?
Before you sign this form, please ____ to check that your name and address are correct.
The teacher received my first draft yesterday and ____ to check the spelling and punctuation before returning it.

meaning: Disappoint someone, especially by failing to do something they trusted you to do.

questions.sentence: My teammates are counting on me to arrive on time. I do not want to ____ by missing the match.
Mum trusted me to water her plants while she was away. I forgot, and I felt sorry that I had ____.
I promised to help my little brother with his project, but I ____ when I went out to play instead.

meaning: Think someone is less important or less worthy of respect than you are.

questions.sentence: Some children ____ because he wears old shoes, but having less money does not make him less worthy of respect.
Mia is new to basketball. We should encourage her and never ____ just because she is still learning.
The wealthy man once ____ because they earned less than he did, but he later learnt to respect them.

meaning: Investigate a problem or situation to find out what happened or what caused it.

questions.sentence: Several library books have gone missing. The librarian will ____ to find out what happened.
Nobody knows why the classroom lights keep going out. An electrician will ____ to discover the cause.
When pupils reported that the school pond was leaking last week, the caretaker ____ to find the cause of the problem.
